Amflow Continues Their Cycling Domination With the UE Carbon Urban E-Bike – Very Enticing Price
25 photos
Photo: Amflow
Back in 2024, DJI, the drone manufacturer, would go on to do something that no one expected: they launched an e-bike system, promising to be the gear to compete with giants like Shimano and Bosch. What they also did was actually launch an entire lineup of bikes that would be equipped with this fresh gear.
The brand is Amflow, and while most of their bikes have been out of reach for the common folk, Amflow just launched their urban commuter, and if I may, they’re really outdoing themselves , yet again.
When Amflow first showed its teeth in 2024, most people couldn’t fathom that a drone manufacturer just spat out full-suspension e-MTBS that could literally compete, even surpass most of what the market had to offer at the time. These babies were equipped with the Avinox, sitting as a perfectly tuned ride for what the Chinese powerhouse was bringing to the table.
Photo: Amflow Well, one trait of the Amflow lineup that kept most people away from the bikes was, sadly, price, or maybe it was the fact that not everyone rides MTBs. So, since 2024, we’ve started to see a sort of progression in terms of pricing for the Amflow beasts, but also the disciplines that their lineup can meet.
While it’s always been the e-MTBs that made the Amflow brand shine, over the past two years, they’ve stepped into adventure biking, whipping up the TL Carbon, a bike that can be found at as low as $3,900, and now, Amflow has unveiled their urban-destined ride, one that is perfectly tuned for the urban landscape and also equipped with the brand’s latest generation Avinox M2 system.
It’s called the Amflow UE Carbon and it’s this brand’s completion of the cycling practices that most riders today are undertaking. Sure, a road bike is missing, but hey, with just two years under their belt, Amflow is already on its third cycling discipline, and I can foresee a road bike in the near future; this is just an assumption and Amflow has not released any word of an electric road bike.
Photo: Amflow As for the UE, this is a whole lot of bike to talk about, and please don’t persecute me for summing up five pages of text into just 10 minutes or so of reading time, but we will be diving waaaaay deeper into an UE since we’re currently testing one as we speak.
For the time being, however, there are a few things that you need to know about this two-wheeler, and the first and most important is the backbone or the frame. At it’s core, the UE is built with a fully carbon fiber frame, one that weighs just 2.35 kg (5.18 lbs).
As we can see, that frame has been optimized for urban use, granting us access to a low-step structure which is essential for comfort and control, especially when you’re riding around with cargo on the front and rear. Amflow has unveiled images with the rear of the UE carrying a child, and the low-step is crucial in ensuring you tip the bike as little as possible during mounting and dismounting.
Photo: Amflow More on the comfort side, a dropper post is available and the handlebar, although not my favorite style, is a sweep-back (gull-wing) one, so very European. This does place the rider in a more upright position, and if I may offer a bit of insight, the riding I’ve done so far with this model has revealed that it is one of the most relaxing postures my body has assumed on an urban bike in some time.
Currently, the frame is a one-size-fits-all, capable of meeting the needs of riders as short as 5 ft 1 in (155 cm) to as much as 6 ft 3 in (190 cm), and does so by supplying riders with two stem lengths that can be easily interchanged and a feature which you’ll read about in the next paragraph.
More on the comfort side of the story, Amflow has decided to add a suspension fork to the UE, granting access to 65 mm of travel and equipped with adjustable damper and lockout. Don’t forget about the dropper post, which, aside from the adjustability, also offer 40 mm of travel to soften up the rear end.
Photo: Amflow Softening up also comes about with the help of Maxxis tires with 2 inches of cross-section, a trait that tells us that the UE can also break the limits of city use and venture onto gravel and hard-pack dirt roads. Magura brakes handle stopping power.
Oh, and you can do all this loaded to the brim with cargo since you have the Avinox M2 motor by your side, assisting us with 125 Nm (92 lb-ft) of torque, suitable for hill grades of up to 30% and is chock-full of hardware and software that constantly analyzes “pedaling intent” to offer the perfect power delivery when you need it.
Keep in mind that all these parameters are adjustable through the Ride app, and while the UE is available in two variations, the standard and Pro, both can tap into fully automatic and electronic shifting. The Pro is powered by a three-speed internal gearbox with the name Avinox on it and a Gates transmission, while the standard is rocking a 10-speed electronic derailleur developed hand-in-hand with TRP.
Photo: Amflow As for speed limits, well, the bikes will clearly be limited to the region where it’s being sold, even though it offers a peak of 1,100 W and the torque I mentioned. Keep in mind that the motor spits our just 45 decibels while under operation, and if I may, it really is whisper quiet.
This brings us to the last few topics on our list today. The first is range, a number which is highly debatable but which Amflow mentions can offer up to 82 miles (132 km) of ride time. With a fast charger, this one can be amped up again from 0-100% in as little as 2 hours and 23 minutes. All very notable traits, if you ask me, especially for a 600 Wh removable pack.
Up next, we have little tricks and abilities like the app I mentioned, which offers an insane amount of control over parameters, Auto Boost function, heart rate tracking, Apple Find My, and so much more.
Photo: Amflow Some functions can be tampered with via the touchscreen display, and we also have audio alerts in case someone’s trying to snag your baby, integrated lighting and rear-wheel lock, and the cargo racks. Don’t forget about the wireless charger that’s also available.
Last but not least, we have ourselves the most-important question of all: How much are we being asked to drop on this urban carbon fiber goodness? Well, remember that I mentioned that Amflow is aiming on releasing more affordable rides, with the standard UE selling for just $3,500 and the Pro for $3,900 (~€3,500). Not bad, if you ask me, and a price that some folks are sure to consider.
